Context: StarRocks-on-Sirius (GPU SQL engine inside a StarRocks compute node, "CN"). Branch demo/q1q6-integration-plus-fixes (worktree /home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/demo-plus, read-only for you) = the dev-based carve of the multi-CN work plus fix 1 (engine OOM fail-fast), fix 2 (per-query parked-output bookkeeping, cancel teardown) and fix 4 (fragment fusion, knob SIRIUS_CN_FRAGMENT_FUSION default leaf). Fix 3 (FILES() cardinalities) is NOT on this branch. Tables are unpinned FILES() scans.
Runs (SF1000 decimal TPC-H, 100 GiB pool per CN, Quent on): /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/demoplus/arms/dp-cn4 (4 CNs, all 22 queries, cold + 2 warm) and /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/demoplus/arms/dp-cn1-six (1 CN, q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21), plus /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/demoplus/arms/dp-cn4-six-stg48 (the six at 4 CNs with a 48 GiB staging arena and a 90 GiB pool, after they failed at 4 CNs with the default 16 GiB arena: 'exchange staging arena exhausted ... 31-47 leases outstanding holding ~16-17 GB', see dp-cn4/runs/q05.r0.err). Each arm dir has runs/runs.csv and runs/qNN.rK.out/.err, cluster.log, engine-.cnN.log, quent/ (raw), cnlog.txt/json (cnlog_extract.py: fragments, declared cardinalities, nixl transmits, OOM reschedules, futile aborts, fix2/fix4 counters), quent.txt/json (quent_bp.py), compare.txt (oracle).
Baselines: /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/sf1000/cn4 and /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/sf1000/cn1 (same box, yesterday, branch perf/profile-sf1000 = feat/pin-table-cn + flags, unpinned; /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/sf1000/results.md, cn4-cnlog.txt, cn4-quent.txt, card-compare-cn4.txt, survey/plan-summary*.txt), /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/sf1000/standalone-failed (standalone Sirius on the six), and the user's reference /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/demoplus/reference-pin-table-cn.md (feat/pin-table-cn with tables PINNED in GPU memory, 1/2/4/8 CNs; not the same I/O path). Merged table: /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/demoplus/compare-ref.md. The user also ran this branch on a 2x RTX PRO 6000 box (2 CNs, NIXL): /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/demoplus/reference-2cn-rtxpro6000.md, where q05 q08 q09 q18 fail with OOM and q17 q21 fail (cause not shown); the user wants to know WHY those six fail with more than one CN and what is needed, noting that feat/pin-table-cn (tables pinned in GPU memory) ran most of them. Tools: /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/sf1000/cnlog_extract.py, quent_bp.py, card_compare.py, results_table.py, /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/quent_summary.py. The SF1000 report from yesterday: /home/prestouser/.claude/plans/starrocks-sirius-perf/sf1000-planning-cardinality-backpressure.md; fix specs: /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/*-SPEC.md.
Rules: do not modify any source tree, do not start clusters or GPU jobs, write only under /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/demoplus/agent-notes/. Measured vs inference, every number with its file.

Refute this finding from the measurements and, where it names a mechanism, from the source: {
 "id": "F4-pin-table-cn-same-exchange-bigger-arena",
 "claim": "feat/pin-table-cn does not avoid the shuffle: its engine and transport have the identical receiver-first, hold-until-last-destination, copy-at-receiver exchange, and its DrainTicket/dispatch_then_join (C8) is an RPC-path latency overlap that the plan itself calls a pure optimisation with wire order unchanged (the demo arms ran the equivalent SIRIUS_CN_ASYNC_SENDER_DISPATCH=1). Pinning replaces the FILES() read, not the DATA_STREAM_SINK. The pinned reference differs by configuration: its SF1000 defaults are GPU_MEM=128GiB STAGING=32GiB, twice the demo arena, and the reference's dagger pattern (q08 and q09 daggered at 4 CN, q05 clean at 4 CN, q08 clean at 8 CN) is consistent with the 34.4 GB arena bound for q05/q08/q09 at N<=4; q21@4CN, q09@8CN and the clean 1-CN q18 are not explained by this arithmetic and the pinned runs' logs are not in the bundle.",
 "evidence": [
  "C/experimental/starrocks/src/engine.rs:275 ('One request at a time'), :403 ('drops when the LAST destination releases'), :624-639 (push_packed at receiver time); compute_node_service.rs:96-148,276 DrainTicket/SenderDrains/dispatch_then_join",
  "~/.claude/plans/i-want-to-create-golden-crane-appendix.md:507,1823,2069-2071: C8 'dispatch a local receiver before joining the remote drains ... Pure optimization (3x30ms per CN on q14 SF500); wire order unchanged'",
  "C/bench/gb200-4gpu/SIRIUS-TUNING-RUNBOOK.md:98 SF1000 row GPU_MEM 128 GiB STAGING 32 GiB; reference-pin-table-cn.md dagger cells q05 1-2CN, q08 1-4CN, q09 1-8CN, q21 1-4CN",
  "capture-arm.sh: SIRIUS_CN_ASYNC_SENDER_DISPATCH=1 exported in every demo arm"
 ],
 "confidence": "medium",
 "impact": "Rules out 'carve more of feat/pin-table-cn' (pinning, C8) as a remedy for the six; the difference the user saw is mostly arena size plus whatever the pinned pool budget allows, not a different data path for the exchange.",
 "task": "why-six-fail-multi-cn"
}
Default to refuted=true only with a concrete contradiction.

## 1. `pipeline_dop` is the first-order FE knob

`engine-a.env` already records the formula:

```
pipeline_dop = min(max_pipeline_dop=64, avgNumCoresOfBe / 2)
```

Each CN is `--physcpubind` to 36 cores, so `SHOW COMPUTE NODES` reports `CpuCores: 36`.
Auto DOP is **18**.

`2NODE-REPLICATE.md` pinned `pipeline_dop=36` because that recipe's 1 CN per host used
`--physcpubind=0-71` (72 cores → auto 36). The 8-GPU launch cargo-culted 36 onto 36-core CNs.

Over-reporting cores, in the same file: more fragment instances → smaller batches → more
exchange RPCs, and each CN has one blocking transport thread. CPU is not the scan bottleneck
on this path.

**SF1000 8-CN: `SET GLOBAL pipeline_dop=18`.** Do not use 36.

## 2. Staging shrinks when N grows

Measured on 8× A100 (`bench/a100x8/TUNING.md`): fewer GPUs need a **bigger** arena. SF500
closed at 12 GiB staging / 8 CNs vs 24 GiB / 4 CNs. The GB200 4-CN SF1000 preset (32 GiB)

1 CN: fix 4 splices the lineitem leaf into the join fragment (`fix4_fused` on every row of `dp-cn1-six/cnlog.txt`), so there is no exchange for lineitem and DuckDB's optimizer makes it the probe (the standalone shape: `perf/sf1000/standalone-failed/runs/q05.explain.txt:50-61`, P1). At 4 CNs every shuffle receiver expects 4 senders and nothing fuses, so the lineitem projection is materialised whole across the cluster, which is the B1 mechanism at N > 1.

### 2.7 What feat/pin-table-cn changes, and what it does not

The exchange design is identical on `feat/pin-table-cn` (`C/experimental/starrocks/src`): one engine request at a time (`engine.rs:275`), parked output held until the last destination releases (`engine.rs:403`), inbound frames pushed and copied at receiver time (`engine.rs:624-639`). `DrainTicket`/`SenderDrains`/`dispatch_then_join` (`compute_node_service.rs:96-148, 276`) is the C8 "drain overlap": the plan appendix describes it as "dispatch a local receiver before joining the remote drains ... pure optimization (3x30 ms per CN on q14 SF500); wire order unchanged" (`~/.claude/plans/i-want-to-create-golden-crane-appendix.md:507, 1823, 2069-2071`). Pinning replaces the FILES() read (the scan source), not the `DATA_STREAM_SINK`; the FE plan and the shuffle bytes are the same.

rendezvous instead of its *rows*; when the receiver becomes ready, splice the sender's `TPlan.nodes`
